title: Exit compositor fullscreen before launching web apps
head: de51dc37d310
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Legacy-config fallback is never reached when the Lua dispatcher is rejected
leads.consequence: With a Hyprland legacy config and a focused fullscreen window, Hyprland returns the string 'Invalid dispatcher' for the Lua-style dispatcher, but hyprctl exits 0. Bash therefore skips `fullscreenstate 0 0`; the launcher still starts the browser, which can take over fullscreen with on_focus_under_fullscreen=1. This is conditional on legacy config, the shipped Omarchy config uses Lua.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Fallback never takes effect; published as a note.

leads.summary: An ordinary focused floating window makes the fullscreen guard miss a fullscreen window behind it
leads.consequence: When a floating overlay on a fullscreen workspace receives focus, activewindow reports that overlay's fullscreen=0. The new branch skips clearing the tiled fullscreen window behind it. Opening a new tiled Chromium web app on that workspace then triggers Hyprland's focus-under-fullscreen takeover, so this path still reproduces the reported inherited fullscreen. Unlike a keyboard-focused layer menu (which retains the prior focused window), a focused floating window really becomes activewindow.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Floating window focused over fullscreen; published (source only).

leads.summary: The guard also discards the user's maximized window state
leads.consequence: Hyprland's fullscreen field has 0=none, 1=maximized and 2=fullscreen. A maximized window meets >0 and is explicitly reset to internal=0, client=0 before every web-app launch (including installed desktop apps and hotkeys). The previously maximized window remains unmaximized even if the new browser fails or closes. This is a scope decision beyond the Firefox fullscreen-video case, not a claim the dispatcher is incorrect.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Maximized mode 1 matched; published with == 2 suggestion.

leads.summary: The new test passes with all fullscreen-handling commands commented out
leads.consequence: The test searches for strings rather than executing the launcher. A plausible broken implementation retaining the new condition and dispatcher strings in comments but never querying or clearing fullscreen passes both advertised assertions, so it cannot detect a regression of its headline behavior. Its Learn menu assertion is unaffected. Add mocked hyprctl/xdg-settings/setsid with an order and call-count assertion for 0, 1, 2, no focused window, dispatch failure and fallback.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Grep-only test; commented-block mutant verified by coordinator grep (triage/mutant-commented.sh) and Opus.

leads.summary: A failed web-app launch still permanently exits the previous window's fullscreen
leads.consequence: The new dispatch runs before resolving whether the selected browser's desktop Exec exists and before invoking uwsm-app. If the app binary is gone, uwsm-app fails, or the URL is rejected, the previous window has already been unfullscreened, and there is no restoration or error about that change. The failed launch has now changed the display without producing a replacement window. This is distinct from intentionally leaving fullscreen for a successful launch.
leads.triage: dropped; Dispatch precedes exec (source-true) so a failed launch leaves prior window unfullscreened; low value edge (missing browser), not material.

leads.summary: Open PR #13241 replaces the exact launcher tail where this PR inserts its guard; integration is required
leads.consequence: #13241 rewrites the browser desktop Exec resolution and the final `exec setsid uwsm-app` command. A three-way merge of the two diverged heads against their common ancestor yields a conflict block spanning the entire new guard and #13241's replacement launcher. Keeping #13241's block as a conflict resolution loses this PR's fix; keeping this PR's block loses wrapped-desktop launch support. The guard must be placed before #13241's final exec after both changes are retained. #13213 separately duplicates the Windows VM chmod change, with conflicts limited to comments and overlapping regression fixtures, so do not count it as a distinct runtime defect.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #13241 open, rewrites same exec line; git merge-file of b5589faa/de51dc37/50d090ba gives one conflict region (triage/merged.sh lines 13-108). #13213 part already in Opus F1.

limits: No live compositor or browser was touched. Hyprland behavior is traced to v0.56.2 source; the floating-window scenario is source-derived rather than reproduced with a live UI.

Windows VM mount tests create /run, /var, /home tmpfs and bind mounts only inside their own user+mount namespaces; no host run was attempted. In review.py's sandbox, the compose test exits at resolve_caller (its real passwd entry's home is hidden), and the root-boundary test reports subordinate-ID namespace unavailable and skips. This is not evidence that the Windows VM runtime test passed; changed mode semantics are supported by GNU coreutils v9.9 doc/perm.texi:583-640 and sandboxed static chmod fixture in plan3/runs/20260928T060820Z-b8055358.
Chromium Esc hint and uwsm-app downstream behavior were not used to establish any verified hunter issue; the main Chromium protocol/design assessment is assigned to the primary reviewer.

flags.claim: The web app is forced tiled (`default/hypr/apps/browser.lua`)
flags.why: browser.lua:2 tags windows by a class regex, and Hyprland 0.56.2 matches rule regexes with RE2::FullMatch (src/desktop/rule/matchEngine/RegexMatchEngine.cpp:16). Omarchy's own rules show web-app classes have the form chrome-<app>-Default (default/hypr/apps/browser.lua:8, default/hypr/apps/bitwarden.lua:3), which the tag regex does not full-match, so browser.lua:4 `tile = true` does not apply to web apps. The conclusion still holds for a different reason: an ordinary xdg toplevel with no parent and no fixed size is not auto-floated (src/managers/XWaylandManager.cpp, shouldBeFloated), so the web app maps tiled and takes over (src/desktop/view/Window.cpp:2435-2439). This error came from my own report (F3a).
flags.fix: Replace with: "The web app opens as an ordinary tiled window and still takes over the fullscreen, so #13170 can still happen." Drop the browser.lua reference.
flags.disposition: fixed; dropped browser.lua forced-tiled claim; 'opens as an ordinary tiled window'

flags.claim: Suggested change: read `hasfullscreen` and `id` from `hyprctl activeworkspace -j` and clear fullscreen only when that workspace has one
flags.why: Three defects in the recipe. (1) `activeworkspace` returns the focused monitor's m_activeWorkspace and never the open special workspace (src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp:578-589), which contradicts the draft's own parenthetical and the map target (Window.cpp:2073). (2) `hasfullscreen` is Fullscreen::controller()->hasFullscreen(w) (HyprCtl.cpp:511), which is true for maximized too (src/managers/fullscreen/handler/FullscreenHandler.cpp:57-59), so it would reintroduce the maximized problem the previous section fixes with `== 2`. (3) The existing dispatch targets the focused window (LuaBindingsDispatchers.cpp:555-556), so clearing another window's fullscreen needs a `window` selector (supported: pushWindowUpval, LuaBindingsInternal.cpp:323-331; same selector form as bin/omarchy-launch-or-focus:16).
flags.fix: Replace the example with: "For example, take the focused monitor's `specialWorkspace.id` (or `activeWorkspace.id` when that is 0) from `hyprctl monitors -j`, find a window on that workspace with `.fullscreen == 2` in `hyprctl clients -j`, and clear it with `hl.dsp.window.fullscreen_state({ internal = 0, client = 0, window = \"address:0x…\" })`. This approach is untested."
flags.disposition: fixed; activeworkspace recipe replaced with monitors -j special/active id + clients -j .fullscreen == 2 + window address selector; still marked untested

flags.claim: Moving the mouse changes the focused monitor while keyboard focus can stay on a fullscreen window on the other monitor.
flags.why: Lost qualifier. Omarchy sets follow_mouse = 1 (default/hypr/input.lua:57), so hovering a window on monitor B focuses it. Keyboard focus stays on A's window only when the pointer on B is over no window, e.g. an empty workspace: no surface keeps the focused window (src/managers/input/InputManager.cpp:623), and a background layer without keyboard interactivity does not take focus (InputManager.cpp:733-736). My report said "the cursor rests on an empty workspace on monitor B".
flags.fix: "Moving the mouse onto an empty workspace on monitor B focuses that monitor while keyboard focus stays on a fullscreen window on monitor A."
flags.disposition: fixed; restored 'onto an empty workspace on monitor B' qualifier

flags.claim: Table row: neither (`0`) | Merge-base: web app opens tiled | This PR: unchanged
flags.why: At the merge-base the web app opens tiled only if no window on the target workspace is fullscreen or maximized. The draft's own next section (floating window focused over a fullscreen window) is a `0` case where the merge-base web app takes over. Internal inconsistency, not a factual error in the PR column.
flags.fix: Add a qualifier to the row, e.g. "neither (`0`)¹" with "¹ and no other window on that workspace is fullscreen; see the next section", or change the Merge-base cell to "web app opens tiled (unless another window on the workspace is fullscreen)".
flags.disposition: fixed; table row 0: '(unless another window on the workspace is fullscreen; see the next section)'

flags.claim: A maximized Chromium window does not have the Escape-hint problem from #13170.
flags.why: Chromium's fullscreen-bubble behaviour was not read from Chromium source or run. What is verified is the Hyprland side: on take-over of a maximized workspace, the web app gets internal mode MAXIMIZED (Window.cpp:2439) and, with syncFullscreen on (WindowRuleApplicator.hpp:110; FullscreenController.cpp:380-389), client state MAXIMIZED, so it is never told it is fullscreen. Low risk, but the sentence states a Chromium behaviour.
flags.fix: "In that case Hyprland hands the web app a maximized state, not fullscreen, so the #13170 fullscreen state does not arise."
flags.disposition: fixed; Chromium claim replaced with Hyprland-side statement (maximized handed over, not fullscreen)

# RETRO: PR #13476

## What worked
- Parallel start: the Sol hunt finished in 18 minutes and the Opus review in about 21 minutes. Four of the six hunter leads corroborated Opus findings; one (#13241 conflict) was new and verified with a three-way `git merge-file`.
- The Opus self-check caught two real errors in the draft. The `browser.lua` tile rule does not match web-app classes, and the suggested `activeworkspace` recipe missed special workspaces, counted maximized and targeted the wrong window. It also caught two lost qualifiers (the empty-workspace condition, and the table row for mode 0).

## Friction
- The coordinator-authored suggested recipe (activeworkspace) was not in Opus's evidence and was wrong. Suggested commands that go beyond reviewer evidence should be run past the reviewer before drafting, or left generic.
- The Opus report and `draft-check.md` both arrived as handbacks (Write refused), as documented; `save-handback` handled both.
- The auto-mode classifier gave repeated "no verdict" errors on Bash near the editorial check step. They were transient.

## Carry forward
- Same author's PR #13477 carries the same Windows VM commit `2b4b0eba`. That PR belongs to another team; noted only as a public fact.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** For the flow reported in #13170 (a Firefox video fullscreen, then **Learn → Omarchy**), the launcher change prevents Hyprland from handing fullscreen to the new Chromium `--app` window. This is established from Hyprland 0.56.2 source and a stubbed `hyprctl` run, not a live session. The web-app change has two scope gaps and a test that only greps the source. The PR also carries an unrelated Windows VM commit that duplicates open PR #13213.

### Unrelated Windows VM commit is bundled in

Commit `2b4b0eba` ("Clear setgid when hardening Windows VM mount folders") changes `bin/omarchy-windows-vm` and three Windows VM tests. The PR description and #13170 do not mention it. Open PR #13213 makes the same `chmod 00700` change at both call sites.

**Verified:** The change itself is correct. GNU chmod keeps a directory's setgid bit for `chmod 0700` and clears it for `chmod 00700` (five or more octal digits), as documented in coreutils `doc/perm.texi`. In a sandboxed relaunch probe with the share seeded at mode 2777, `prepare_caller_mounts` failed silently at the merge-base (mode left at 2700) and succeeded on this head (mode 700). The head's `windows-vm-test.sh` and `windows-vm-compose-test.sh` additions fail against the merge-base and pass on the head. The compose test needed a stubbed passwd lookup in the sandbox, and `windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh` was not executed.

**Impact:** This PR and #13213 carry the same fix, and this PR's description does not cover what it changes. The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks for atomic commits that do not mix unrelated work.

**Suggested change:** Drop `2b4b0eba` from this PR and leave the setgid fix to #13213 or a separate PR.

### The check also fires for maximized windows

`activewindow -j` reports `.fullscreen` as Hyprland's internal mode: `0` none, `1` maximized, `2` fullscreen (`FullscreenController.hpp`). The condition `(.fullscreen // 0) > 0` therefore also matches a window maximized with **SUPER + ALT + F** ("Full width"). In that case Hyprland hands the web app a maximized state, not fullscreen, so the #13170 fullscreen state does not arise.

| Focused window before launch | Merge-base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| fullscreen (`2`) | web app takes over fullscreen (#13170) | fullscreen cleared, web app opens tiled |
| maximized (`1`) | web app takes over maximized | maximized cleared, web app opens tiled |
| neither (`0`) | web app opens tiled (unless another window on the workspace is fullscreen; see the next section) | unchanged |

**Impact:** Opening any web app (keybinding, menu entry or desktop file) from a maximized window now takes the workspace out of maximized mode, which #13170 does not require.

**Suggested change:** Match only real fullscreen: `jq -e '(.fullscreen // 0) == 2'`.

### The focused window is not always the window the new app would take over from

Hyprland maps the new window onto the focused **monitor's** active workspace, but the guard looks only at the focused **window**. Two cases follow from Hyprland source; neither was reproduced live:

- **Floating window focused over a fullscreen window.** Hyprland lets a floating window take focus above a fullscreen window without ending that fullscreen. `activewindow` then reports the floating window with `fullscreen: 0`, so the guard does nothing. The web app opens as an ordinary tiled window and still takes over the fullscreen, so #13170 can still happen.
- **Two monitors.** Moving the mouse onto an empty workspace on monitor B focuses that monitor while keyboard focus stays on a fullscreen window on monitor A. The guard then clears fullscreen on monitor A even though the web app opens on monitor B, where nothing would have been handed over. At the merge-base, monitor A stays fullscreen.

**Impact:** Edge cases: the fix is skipped in the first and removes fullscreen unnecessarily in the second.

**Suggested change:** Check the fullscreen state of the workspace the new window will open on (the focused monitor's active special or regular workspace) rather than the focused window's. For example, take the focused monitor's `specialWorkspace.id` (or `activeWorkspace.id` when that is 0) from `hyprctl monitors -j`, find a window on that workspace with `.fullscreen == 2` in `hyprctl clients -j`, and clear it with `hl.dsp.window.fullscreen_state({ internal = 0, client = 0, window = "address:0x…" })`. This approach is untested.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/launch-webapp-fullscreen-test.sh` only greps `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp` for strings. With the whole new `if … fi` block commented out, all four patterns still match, so the test would still pass. The test also does not check that the dispatch comes before `exec`. `test/shell.d/hyprland-window-test.sh` already stubs `hyprctl`, and `docs/testing.md` recommends "Stub the world, run the real code". A behavioural version would run the launcher with stub `hyprctl` and `uwsm-app` and assert these cases:

- `fullscreen: 2` logs the dispatch before the launch.
- `0`, `{}` or no `hyprctl` logs no dispatch and still launches (add `1` if the `== 2` change above is adopted).

**Note on the fallback:** The `|| hyprctl dispatch fullscreenstate 0 0` fallback never takes effect in Hyprland 0.56.2. With a Lua config the legacy string is also parsed as Lua and fails. With a legacy config the Lua string gets an `Invalid dispatcher` reply, but `hyprctl` still exits 0, so the `||` branch never runs. The same pattern already exists in `bin/omarchy-hyprland-window-tiled-fullscreen-toggle`, but the new test asserts the fallback as a feature.

**Related open PR:** #13241 rewrites the same `exec` line at the end of `bin/omarchy-launch-webapp`. A three-way merge of the two heads against their common ancestor gives one conflict region covering the new fullscreen block, so whichever lands second needs to keep both changes.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of both commits against Hyprland 0.56.2 (the reporter's version), GNU coreutils/gnulib chmod and dockur/windows `samba.sh`. Sandboxed runs used a stubbed `hyprctl` modelling 0.56.2's replies and exit codes, the PR's tests on the head and against the merge-base, and a Windows VM relaunch probe on synthetic directories. No live Hyprland, Chromium, Firefox or Windows VM runs. The floating-window and multi-monitor cases come from source only, and `windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh` was not executed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
